- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp moves; apply downward bias or lag correction.
- After a price spike, model frequently overcorrects or overshoots in next period; dampen forecast by 5–10% relative to peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days moving toward historical mean), model tends to hold or overpredict; adjust downward.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2 day lag correction or reduce first 3–5 values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may overreact; reduce forecast slope or add smoothing factor.
